content:
Jimmy Kimmel continues to mock Donald Trump's ongoing efforts to have his name added to the Kennedy Center.

"Yesterday, members of the Kennedy Center board of directors — handpicked by Trump himself — voted to temporarily shut down the center for renovations, right after a judge ruled they couldn't add Trump's name to the building without congressional approval," Kimmel said during his monologue on Wednesday night.

"So this big baby is now saying that if the Supreme Court doesn't overturn that ruling and put his name next to Kennedy's, then no renovations will happen," the late-night host added.

Kimmel said the president is now adding his name to "everything in town."

"The one thing he doesn't want to put his name on right now is his eldest son, Don Jr.," Kimmel said, referring to the president's firstborn.

He then joked that Trump is "holding the building hostage." He added: "They should really just rename it the Melania Trump Kennedy Center," drawing laughter from the studio audience.

Trump wrote on Truth Social that he was closing the center for "safety reasons," after a federal judge rejected his application to add the "needless and self-aggrandizing" phrase "renovated and restored by President Trump" to the building's exterior.

Trump wrote in a Tuesday post: "The renovation and rebuilding project is of such magnitude and complexity that it cannot be undertaken until a ruling is made by the Washington D.C. Circuit Court of Appeals on the naming decision passed by the Board." He then made his position even clearer.

"If the ruling comes back negative — which it shouldn't — and isn't overturned by the United States Supreme Court, the rebuilding and renovation of the Kennedy Center will not happen," he said.

The late President Kennedy's niece, Maria Shriver, had a lot to say about Trump's attempts to permanently associate his name with that of her late uncle.

Shriver wrote earlier this week on X: "I'm truly stunned by these remarks from Trump. A sitting president refusing to allow any public building to be renovated unless he can put his name on it first... What a sad state of affairs. A tragedy."

She criticized Trump for being "small-minded" and "narcissistic," while adding that "truly great people, people who devote themselves to public service and the public good, don't behave this way."

She said: "Imagine spending all your time and energy on this kind of thing while everyday Americans struggle to get by, facing problems with healthcare, gas prices, rent, and food. Imagine spending all your days on this, while there is a war going on under your administration."
